correctness.rationale: For any nondegenerate equilateral triangle split into exactly two closed convex equal-area pieces, the cut is a chord. With t,u measured along two sides, tu=1/2, after reflection 1/√2≤t≤1, u=1/(2t). Three necessary supporting halfplanes for the piece containing side BC force r≤√3(t−1/2)/(2(2t−u+L)), while BC forces R≥1/2. The two exact factorization identities L²−3t²/4=(t−1/t)²/4≥0 and ((2+√3/2)t−u−((3+√3)/2)(2t−1))=(1−t)((1+√3/2)t−1/2)/t≥0 imply strict bound unless t=1. At t=1 the two right triangles have R=1/2 and r=(√3−1)/4, giving exactly three symmetry-related median optimizers. Independently verified critical symbolic identities and continuous-range sample inequality; sampling is not the continuous proof.

value.rationale: The equal-area two-piece equilateral benchmark settles a natural minimal bisection problem for roundness with an exact sharp constant and complete equality classification. It calibrates universal fat-part partition theory in its first nontrivial two-piece case, and is not a mechanically implied single-triangle formula since one piece may be quadrilateral.

scientific_limitations: Exactly two full-dimensional convex parts of equal area, in a Euclidean equilateral triangle.
No universal best partition fatness for general convex bodies, and no claim about three-or-more pieces.
